spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of
 the K
ephal
aia Chapter
 on
 the Light
 Mind

---


**
¶1.
** You
 have been
 told
 that Divine
 Wisdom shall
 descend and unite
 with the regenerate.
 It is itself one
 among
 the divine qualities, and the fullness
 of divine qualities accompan
ies it. You
 have also
 been told:
 when
 it enters
 within
 the natural mind and restrains the inherited
 selfhood by
 the
 full
ness of its spiritual
 faculties, it establ
ishes those
 faculties over the self
hood within
 the five capacities of the natural mind
.

**¶2.**
 Then
 where
 does Divine Wisdom reside, given
 that the inherited selfhood is restrained
 within the natural mind?
 For
 I perce
ive that disturbances of evil still
 arise within, from time to time,
 despite this
 restraint.

**¶3
.** And second
ly I
 ask: if Divine Wisdom is infinite
 and unchanging, how can it desc
end and
 manifest
 within
 the fin
itude of the natural
 mind?


**¶4.**
 Thirdly I
 wish
 to understand
: if Divine Wisdom is holy and
 pure, how can it endure the
 corruption of the natural mind?

**
¶5.**
 Fourthly:
 if truly
 Divine Wisdom dwells within the regener
ate,
 why
 is
 its essential nature not manifest outwardly
 to us
, as it truly is?

**
¶9
.** All that you have disclosed,
 you have set before us
. Yet
 I desire to know Divine
 Wisdom in its own essential
 nature.

---


**¶11
.** All
 fals
ity — when the adversary of wisdom
 constructed it — was constructed after the image
 of the Divine Human form
. The governing principle of this false order
 is the origin of its external
 tru
ths. Its connective faculty
 is the junction
 of those external truths. Its recept
ive capacity
 is the fullness of its unfol
ded external truths. Its structural
 supports
 are all
 the degrees of its apparent understanding. Its
 central knowledges are the sphere of
 all natural knowledges and their ordered
 cycles. The fac
ulties that
 descend from these knowledges toward
 the lower will
 extend from the sphere of kn
owledges to the boundaries of the four
 states
 of the natural mind. Its
 generative power is the three degrees of
 the natural mind that lie below, r
esting upon
 the sustaining faculty at the lowest foundation
. And its lowest supports extend
 down to the ground upon which the
 sustaining faculty stands
 firm
.

**¶12.**
 The will of this false order
 is humanity itself. Its natural aff
ections are the four
-footed creatures. Its rational
 thoughts are the winged things
 that move through the air of
 understanding
. Its gathered natural
 knowledges are the things
 that
 swim
 through
 the waters of memory-
truth
. Its lowest
 sensory
 affections are the
 things
 that creep upon the ground of the
 external mind. Its outermost appearance
 is the boundary wall
 that encloses the pier
cing intensity of self-love. Its
 containing forms hold that consuming
 self
-love. Its bitt
erness is hatred
. Its interior bread
th is the vast
 expanse of world
ly states. Its channels carry
 all
 the springs
 and sources of truth throughout the whole.


*
[
Several
 correspond
ences in the lac
unae resist
 full
 translation;
 what
 surv
ives confirms
 the consistent
 structure:
 each
 organ
 of
 the false
 order corresponds to a spiritual faculty
 or
 state
 inv
erted
 by
 the advers
ary.
]*

**¶13.**
 This
 is how all
 the states of the spiritual order have been
 harmon
ized. The fullness of divine fac
ulties is fast
ened within it;
 they
 are its
 anim
ating life
. The divine creative power and the divine
 mediating presence,
 together
 with the fullness of ever-wak
eful spiritual guardians, sust
ain the
 whole.

**¶14.
** The faculty
 of spiritual illumin
ation —
 the
 love that governs in the highest degree
 of
 the will
 — has been established above in
 the realm
 of the will
. The fullness of the powers of
 heaven
 r
eside
 within the
 faculty
 of spiritual thought
 —
 which
 is faith
 existing
 in the complete
 degree
 of understanding. The faculty of spiritual perception
 — which is insight —
 has
 been set
 in
 its
 place.
 Because
 of
 the enc
ro
achment of sel
fish desire, the faculty of spiritual counsel
 — which is patience — has been appointed
 to govern the
 three active spiritual principles: thought
, love, and truth. Authority
 over the resistance of evil has been given
 to it
. The sust
aining faculty of consideration
 — which is wisdom at
 the lowest foundation — has been established below
, up
holding all that rests upon it
.

**¶15.**
 Furthermore
, the divine mediating presence refined
 from
 within
 them five living faculties of perception.
 The call
 of divine truth and the will
's responsive obedience were established there
. Together
 they constit
uted twelve
 derivative
 faculties — six from the divine creative
 power and six from the primordial
 human will.

**¶16
.** Furthermore
, the divine mediating presence established within
 them the
 great Divine Wisdom itself
 —
 the central sustaining truth
 — the
 image of the fully
 regenerate human
.


**¶17.** Furthermore
, the newly
-desc
ending Divine
 Truth
 was set
 in place
 —
 the living image of the active
 Word
, the unity of truth spoken
 and truth received in
 ob
edience.


**¶18.** These
 states
 of
 spiritual order, both
 in
 higher and lower degrees, have been made
 strong
, so that each
 one
 remains
 secure
 within
 the
 sphere of its governance, and
 neither rebellion of
 evil nor de
ception of falsity may
 arise within its domain
.

---


**¶19.** And
 be
hold: the faculty of spiritual illumination
 is established in the governing
 love
, in the state above the confin
ement of the restrained evils,
 for
 it reduces to
 nothing all the obscurity of spiritual death
. Yet
 a
 deception arose
, and a rebellion. Evil produced prem
ature and disordered spiritual forms that
 became entangled with the spiritual life
. These
 became min
gled with the wisdom that had
 been directed
 toward
 the divine
 mediating presence. The
 disturbance passed through the third
 degree of understanding
, above
 the station of spiritual illumination. From
 there also
 it became ent
angled with wisdom. It was separated
 and descended into the barren
 will and the recept
ive understanding of the natural mind. In
 the barren will it fashioned false
 perceptions; and
 in the gathered
 natural knowledges it immediately
 took
 form
 and raised a great rebellion.

**
¶20.** And
 behold: the faculty of spiritual thought
,
 which is faith, is established in the
 third degree of understanding.
 It
 was
 prov
oked to
 w
rath. A rebellion occurred — deception
 and anger
 arose within
 its
 domain. The guardian perceptions of the
 higher mind descended into the natural mind within
 its domain and
 committed
 all manner of tre
achery. They introduced
 cunning knowledges into the external
 world and exposed interior spiritual truths to
 the natural mind —
 an
 act
 of prof
anation.
 Rebellion
 and destruction
 arose in the natural mind.

**
¶21.** The
 faculty of spiritual perception
 was established in its domain. And a
 deception occurred within its domain — when
 the premature and disordered spiritual
 forms descended
 into the natural mind. They fash
ioned the
 first
 natural
 understanding and the first natural will. They
 generated
 these faculties so as to rule through
 them in the external world. They produced
 every form of selfish desire upon
 the ground of the natural mind. The
 entire
 natural mind was filled with their desire.


**¶22.** Again
, in
 the domain of spiritual counsel, which is
 patience —
 the faculty
 governing
 the three active principles
 — within the three degrees of the natural
 mind, disturbance and affl
iction arose,
 for
 the faculties were constricted and
 oppressed. After the divine mediating
 presence revealed
 its nature, the pathways were
 closed
 and the ascent of these principles was
 impeded:
 the up
ward movement of spiritual
 thought
, truth
, and love was obstructed.


**¶23.** Again
, in the domain of the
 sust
aining faculty of wisdom at the lowest foundation
,
 a
 rebellion arose from
 the deepest states of evil
 below
. The structural
 bonds
 beneath were loos
ened, threatening the very foundation.


---


**¶24.** Because
 of the fundamental disturbance that
 occurred in the domain
 of spiritual illumination, the central
 sustaining truth came
 forth as its helper. It bore up
 beneath
 all the bur
dens of the spiritual order.


**¶25.**
 Convers
ely, because
 of the de
ception and rebellion in
 the domain of spiritual thought —
 the guardian
 perceptions that
 had descended from the
 higher mind into
 the natural mind — four
 divine powers were summoned.
 They restrained the fallen
 per
ceptions with permanent bonds in the confin
ement of those
 in utter falsity. They removed
 their
 offspring
 from the natural mind.

**
¶26.** Then
 again
, the
 prem
ature and disordered forms
 descended
 in the domain of spiritual perception and produced
 the first natural understanding and the first natural
 will. Because
 of this great deception and the
 hidden
 working
 of evil
, Divine Truth
 was sent forth, in
 answer to the sup
plication of the fullness of spiritual fac
ulties. It united with
 them
 and restrained the disordered forms
,
 establishing
 them beneath
 the will
 of the first
 natural understanding.

**¶27
.** Also
, because
 of the fundamental
 disturbance in the three
 degrees of the natural mind — the path
ways being
 obstructed and the springs
 of spiritual thought
, truth, and love being blocked —
 Divine Truth cast
 itself
 down and united
 with the natural
 will. It straight
ened the path
ways of
 thought
, truth, and love. It opened
 their springs
 and set
 in
 order the way
 of their
 ascent.

**¶28
.** Again
:
 because
 the
 lowest ground of the natural mind beneath the
 sustaining faculty had
 been loos
ened from
 its
 found
ational bonds
, Divine
 Truth descended still
 further, united
 with the natural will, until
 it reached that lowest place
. It restored
 and strength
ened the foundational bonds beneath.
 Then it
 returned and
 asc
ended again
 to its proper state
 of
 rest
.

---


**¶29.**
 Be
hold all
 the domains
 of spiritual
 governance,
 those
 in which
 the great
 divine faculties are sovereign
, watching
 over them. Rebellions of
 evil and deceptions of falsity have
 occurred
 within them, from time to time,
 with great
 labor
 and sustained
 a
bas
ement,
 until
 they
 subd
ued the opposing
 powers.

**¶30.
** So
 also is the natural
 mind.
 A
 mighty
 divine
 power dw
ells here
, even
 though the natural mind is small in
 its
 capacity
. Nevertheless
, evil
 dw
ells within,
 and the inherited selfhood that
 inhab
its it.
 This selfhood is fierce and deeply
 cun
ning — until
 Divine Wisdom discovers
 the
 means
 to
 sub
due the
 natural mind and govern
 it according to the divine will.


**¶31.** Just
 as in
 the mac
rocosmic
 domains
 of the greater divine
 faculties —
 those
 that govern the whole spiritual order — dist
urbances and de
ceptions have occurred
 from
 time to time in
 that
 greater
 order, so also within
 the domain
 of Divine
 Wisdom,
 which
 is the natural
 mind:
 evil
 raises
 its ag
itations
 within
 the natural mind from time to time.


**¶32.** Now
 understand
: the
 divine
 fac
ulties are good
.
 The beginning
 and the end are open
 to their perception. All that they do
 is done with
 just
 disc
ernment. Indeed
, for
 this
 reason they may permit evil to init
iate its deception and act according to
 its desire for a moment. Then
 they
 seize upon it — for
 they have
 acted
 from
 the
 first with righteous f
ores
ight.

**¶33.
** And
 behold: these
 divine
 faculties, though
 they are great and
 mighty
, each
 one is contracted
 and pressed
 within the place
 where it is appointed
 —
 like
 per
ceptions holding
 fast to
 their
 deep
est interior
 truth
. Just
 so
, each
 divine
 faculty has
 held
 fast to its
 deep
est interior truth within
 its
 domain, according
 to the nature of the state in which
 it is established,
 bearing
 up under
 all things
.

---


**¶35
.** Evil
 bound
 the
 spiritual
 life
 within
 the five capacities of the natural mind
. It
 bound the will
 in
 the foundational structure. It bound the
 understanding
 in the conn
ective reasoning
. It bound the perception in the interior
 channels. It bound the deliberation in
 the proprium of
 the will
. It bound the reflective wisdom in
 the outermost natural
 appearances.

**¶36.
** Evil
 established
 its own five count
erf
eit faculties:
 its own will upon the will
 of
 the
 spiritual
 life;
 its own understanding upon the understanding of the
 spiritual life; its own perception upon the
 perception of the spiritual life; its own
 deliberation upon the deliberation of the
 spiritual life; its own reflective wisdom
 upon the reflective wisdom of the spiritual
 life.
 It
 set
 its
 five
 governing
 powers and authorities upon the five capac
ities of the spiritual
 life, which it had drawn in
ward and bound within the proprium.


**¶37.** The
 spiritual
 life took
 on
 fals
ity and the loss
 of spiritual
 memory
. It forgot its own divine
 essence
, its spiritual
 origin
, and
 its heavenly kindred
. It no
 longer knew the way to
 approach
 the Divine
,
 nor
 how
 to call
 upon it. It became hostile toward
 its
 own divine source
,
 acting
 wick
edly against its
 own wisdom
.

**¶38.**
 Divine
 Wisdom comes
 and
 finds the spiritual life in
 this
 condition
. It assumes
 it
 with
 its wisdom
.
 It becomes
 the
 liber
ator from
 the bonds
 within
 the capac
ities of the natural mind. It loos
ens the will
 of
 the
 spiritual
 life and
 releases
 it
 from the foundational structure. It releases
 the understanding
 of the spiritual life from the connective
 reasoning,
 and bin
ds the understanding
 of evil in the connective reasoning instead
. It releases the perception of the spiritual
 life from the interior channels, and bin
ds the perception of evil in the interior
 channels.
 It loos
ens the deliberation of the spiritual life
 and
 releases it from the prop
rium,
 and binds the deliberation of evil
 in the proprium.
 It releases the reflective wisdom of the
 spiritual life from the outermost natural
 appearances, and binds the reflective
 wisdom of evil in the outermost
 appearances
 instead
.

**¶39.**
 This
 is how Divine Wisdom shall
 lib
erate the fac
ulties of the spiritual life and set them
 free from the five counterfeit fac
ulties of evil. And conversely,
 the
 five
 fac
ulties of evil, which had been un
restrained, it
 shall bind
 fast
.

**
¶40.** Divine
 Wisdom shall restore
 the
 fac
ulties of the spiritual life —
 shape
 them, purify them, and
 build from
 them a regenerate person
, a child of righte
ousness. When
 it fash
ions,
 builds
, and pur
ifies the regener
ate person, it shall bring
 forth five
 great
 living qualities
 from
 its
 own
 five
 great
 qualities
 and place them within the fac
ulties of the regenerate person. It
 shall place its love —
 the essence of the will
 — in
 the
 will
 of
 the regenerate person. It shall place
 faith — the essence of understanding — in
 the understanding of the regenerate person.
 It shall place perf
ection — the essence of perception
 — in the perception of the regenerate
 person. It shall place patience — the
 essence of deliberation — in the deliber
ation of the regenerate person. And
 it shall place wisdom
 — the essence of reflective thought —
 in the reflective thought of the regener
ate person. It shall purify the
 form of truth
 from
 the fals
ity of evil
,
 and inf
use its
 own
 truth
,
 so
 that the regener
ate person is n
ourished and
 strengthened from
 within.

**¶41.
** When Divine Wisdom shall
 bring
 to
 completion the fullness of all goods
 and
 tru
ths within the regenerate person —
 this
 is how its
 wisdom
 operates.
 The
 regenerate person becomes righteous as the
 perfecting advances
.
 Whereas
 formerly
 the person
 was running after worldly things, now
 instead
 the
 person advances
 along
 the true path and ascends to the
 elevated states
 of the eternal spiritual realms.
 And
 so
 the inherited
 selfhood is bound — together
 with its sel
fish desire and its ignor
ance — within the five capacities of
 the natural mind. The spirit
 of falsity is imprisoned
 with them in bond
age and
 severe
 constraint
.

**¶42.**
 The
 regener
ate person governs through
 love, faith, perfection, patience
, and
 wisdom.
 Yet
 the true
 sovereign
 is
 Divine Wisdom itself
, which re
igns over the
 whole according
 to the divine will. While
 the living
 faculties govern
, evil
 remains imprisoned
. Still
, Divine Wisdom is sovereign, and
 affl
iction may arise within the natural mind from
 time to time.

**¶
43.** There
 are occasions
 when evil
 shall rise up with
 its spiritual ignorance and disturb the
 faculty
 of refl
ective wisdom. It clouds
 wisdom
 and understanding. It causes
 truth
 to be divided into doubt within the person
, and the person ut
ters words of ignor
ance and falsity.


---


**¶51
.** Just
 as confusion
 ar
ises in the whole spiritual order, in
 the states governed by the great
 divine faculties —
 so
 also dist
urbance
 comes
 about
,
 from time to time, within the governance
 of Divine Wisdom in the natural mind
.

**¶52.**
 Just
 as the spiritual
 guard
ians are established firmly
 in the spiritual order yet
 are not out
wardly visible, so also Divine
 Wisdom dwells within the natural mind yet
 is not visible
 there
.

**¶53.**
 Just as the greater
 spiritual guardians —
 though
 great
 in
 themselves
 — have
 contracted
 and
 dimin
ished themselves to the measure of the
 task
 appointed
 to each one
,
 so also Divine Wisdom, great
 and
 ex
alted in
 itself, has bent
 down
 and become contracted
 to d
well within the small and lowly natural
 mind.

**¶54.
** Just
 as the divine
 faculties in
 the greater spiritual order are transcendent and
 pure — established within the mingling of
 the whole,
 yet never defiled — so also Divine
 Wisdom: though placed
 within the impure natural mind, it
 remains undefiled.

**
¶55.**
 Be
hold the power and the
 activity of Divine Wisdom —
 how vast it is over all the domains
 of the natural mind. It remains fixed
 in its proper state. It bars all
 the deliberations of the natural mind from
 the deceptions of evil. It sets
 limits for them and distributes them in
 order
. It disposes all things according to
 the divine will.

**¶
57
.** Whoever
 possesses the open interior faculty of spiritual
 sight — to such a one Divine
 Wisdom can become manifest. Whoever lacks
 that faculty cannot perceive it.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: All the error, when the en[e]my of the lights constructed it, he constructed after the likeness of a man. The head of the universe is the beginning of the garments. [H]is neck is the nape of the garm[ents]. His stomach is the five unfolded ones (?), which a[re the fullness] of the garm[e]nts. His ribs are all the firmament[s]. His navel is the sphere of the stars and the signs of the zodiac. And, also, [the par]ts [that] come from his navel to his hip are [the regions] that come from the sphere t[o the corne]rs of the four worlds. His loins are the th[ree eart]hs that are below[, resting] upon the head of the Porter. His [thighs reach] from the [three earths] to the earth upon which the Porter [is stood] firm. His shins and his feet a[re the land of darkness] and the entire zone that belongs [to the depths below.]

His heart is mankind. His liver is the four-footed animals. His lung is the race of birds that [fly in] the air. His spleen is the race of fish that swim in the waters. His kidneys are the world of reptiles that creep [up]on the earth. His outer skin is the wall that [encircles all, which] surrounds the piercing and the great fire. His [bowels are] the vessels of the great fire. His [marrow is the depth] of darkness. His gall is the [bitterness of hatred. His] great intestine is the breadth of the great [expanse] of the worlds. His veins [are] all [the spri]ngs and wells. His e[yes are the two luminaries.] His feet are his [lowest foundation.]

This is how each of the worlds h[ave been ha]rmonised (?). Five gods are fastened in him. [For] they are his soul and his life[. Though] man is a sinner[,] the Living Spirit and the Ambassador [have set over him] the five sleepless guardians.

Furthermore: The Ambassador refined from them five intellectuals of life. Also, the summons and the obedience were situated there. Now, they made six sons of the Living Spirit, together with the six sons of the First Man!
Further: The Ambassador placed in them the great Mind; who is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man.
Furthermore: Jesus the Youth was set there; who is the image of the living word, of the utterance and the obedience.

He has made strong these camps, those above and those below [in all their places], (so that) each one of them will be secure in the circuit of his watch-district, so that neither uprising nor treachery are made in his watch-district.

And look, see! The Keeper of Splendour is set firm in the great mind, in the camp above the prison of the bound ones, for he brings to nothing all the gloom of death. An[d a] treachery came about, and an uprising! The Sin abor[te]d, [it t]angled in with the soul. It became mixed with this light that it expelled toward the image of the Ambassador. It went [up] in the third firmament that is above the watch-t[ower of] the Keeper of Splendour. From that place also it tangled in with the light. It was detached and came down to that which is dry and that which is moist. It [fashio]ned the trees [up]on the dry (land); but in the sea it immediat[ely] took form and made a great uprising in the sea.

Again, look, see! The great King of Honour, who is the thought, he is in the thi[r]d firmament. He is made [to contend] with wrath. And an uprising came about! A treachery and a[n] anger happened in his camp. The watchers of heaven, who came down to the earth in his watch-district, they did all the deeds of treachery. They have revealed crafts in the world and have unveiled to people the mysteries of heaven. An uprising came about, and a destruction, on the earth [and great affliction came] to it.

The Adamant [of Light is] the fulfillment. He is set firm upo[n his watch;] and a treachery came about in his camp; the occasion when the abortions fell to the earth. They formed Adam and Eve. They begat them so as to reign through them in the world. They fashioned every object of lust upon the earth. The entire world was filled by their lust.

Once again: In the watch of the great King of Glory, wh[o] is the great counsel, he who exercises authority over the thre[e] wheels. A [dis]turbance came about, and an affliction, for [they were greatly] pained and oppressed in the three earths. After the Ambassador displayed his image, the paths closed to their [springs, and] their ascent was impeded by them[; neither could] the w[ind], the water, and the fire ascend on them.

[O]nce again: In the watch of the Porter, he who humiliates [all beneath. An] uprising of the abysses below [came about. He was] bent, the fastenings underneath were loosened [and shaken] in the foundation below.

On account of the earthquake that happened in the watch of the Keeper of Splen[dour], the Pillar of Glory came forth; as it [became the] helper of the Keeper of Splendour. It bore up under all [burden]s.

Conversely, because of the treachery and the uprising that happened in the watch of the great King of Honour, which is the watchers who came down to earth from the heavens; four angels were called upon about them. They bound the watche[r]s with an eternal chain, in the prison of the blackened ones (?). [Th]ey obliterated their children from upon the earth.

[Th]en, again, the abortions descended in the watch of the Adamant and begat Adam and Eve; because of that great treachery wh[ich] happened, and the mystery of wickedness, he sent Jesus [in answer to] the prayer of the five sons. He assumed them [and he restrained] the abortions. He fastened them beneath the [power of] the mind of Adam.

Also, because of the earthquake that happened in these three earths, and in that the paths were hindered and the springs of wind and water and fire were impeded, Jesus cast himself down. He assumed Eve; and he straightened the tracks of the [win]d, the water, and the fire. He opened the springs for them, and he set [in ord]er the path of their ascent.

Once [again]: Since the earth beneath the Porter was loose[ned from] the fastenings that [held it firm;] because of this too Jesus went down, assuming [Ev]e until he reached tha[t] place. [H]e set in [or]der and stre[ng]th[ened] the fastenings beneath. He returned, [he came] up to his [place of] rest.

Look at all these watches of the zon[e], the ones in which these great gods are master, w[atch]ing over them [ceaselessly]. Uprisings have happened, and treachery, in them. The [gods have laboured] in them from time to time; with a great hum[iliati]on, until they humbled the powers of the enmity.

So also is this body! A mighty power lives here, even if it is small in its stature. Nevertheless, Sin dwells within, and the old man who is lodged in it. Certainly he is cruel, with great cunning; until the Lig/ht Mind finds how to humble this body, and drive it [according to] his pleasure.

Just so, in the w[atch-]districts of his great outer brothers, they who are masters in the zone: in them, in the great body, the earthquake and treachery happened from time to time. So, also, is the watch-district of the Mind, which is the body of the flesh. Sin raises [up], from time to time, its agitations in the body.

Now you, understand thus, that the powers of light are good. The beginning and the end are unveiled to them. All that they do is being done with correct judgement. Indeed, because of this they may permit the enmity to initiate error, and do its pleasure for a moment. Then they seize [upon it, for] they have acted first with a righteous judgement.

And [with resp]ect to this other (question) that you have put forward: How may the Light Mind come, this great and honoured mighty one, and assume this little body of the flesh? Again, look, see! These gods, in that [they] are great and mighty ones. And each one of them is enclosed and hard pressed in this place wherein he is set; like trees holding to their taproot. So also this is how each one of them has held to his taproot in the world, according to the k[ind] of place in which he is set, bearing up till [the consummation.]
(Sin) bound (the soul) in the five members of the body. It bound the mind in bone; the thought in sinew; the insight in vein; the counsel in flesh; the consideration in ski[n].

(Sin) set f[ast] its five powers: its mind upon the mind of the soul; its thought upon the thought of the soul; its insight upon the insight of the soul; its counsel upon the counsel of the soul; its consider[atio]n upon the consideration of the soul. It placed its five [an]gels and authorities upon the five members of the soul, which it had brought in and bound in the flesh. They [rule over it], pronouncing to the soul and continually leading it on to every evil thi[n]g,

(The soul) assumed error and forgetfulness. It for[go]t its essence and its race and its kindred; kn[ow]ing not the door of the place to pray to him, nor call up to him. It became hostile to its father [and to] itself, being wicked [against] its own light [and its own nature.]

The Light Mind comes and finds the soul [in bondage, and comes to] it assuming it in the [power of] its wisdom[. And] he shall become for it [the loosener of] the bonds [of the five] members in the body. He shall loosen the m[ind of the soul and relea]se it from the bone. He shall release the th[ought of the soul] from the sinew; and s[o] bind the thought [of the Sin in] the sinew. He shall release the insight of the soul from the vei[n]; and so bind the insight of the Sin in the vein. [He sh]all loosen the counsel of the soul, and release it from the flesh; and so bind the counsel of the Sin in the flesh. He shall release the consideration of the soul from the skin; and bin[d] the consideration of the Sin in the skin.
This is how he shall release the members of the soul, and make them free from the five members of Sin. Conversely, these five members of Sin, which were loose, he shall bind them.

He shall set right the members of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a new man of them, a child of righteousness. [And] when [he] fashions and const[r]ucts and purifies the new man; then he shall bring forth five great living members out from the five great memb[ers]. And he places them in the members of the new man. He shall place his m[ind], which is love, in the mind of the new man. Also, the th[oug]ht, which is faith, he shall pl[ace in] the thought of the new man; whom he shall purify. His insight, which [is perfection, he shall place] in the insight of the new man. His counsel, which [is] patience, he shall place in his counsel. Also, [w]isdom, which is his consideration, in the consideration of the new m[an]. He shall make the image of the word pure from the word of Sin; and he adds to it his word, so that his [word] becomes nourisher and strengthener [of the new man.]

Now, when he shall perf[ect and purify the tw]elve members. This [is the work of his love] and his wisdom. His [new man] becomes righteous, as he perf[ects him.] While formerly he was running [after the world,] but instead of this, now he runs [upon] his road and his path and his [ascent;] also [he mounts up] to the heights, to the great aeons [of light; and] thus the old man is bound in the [body,] and his lust, his [wrath, and] his foolishness in these five members of the bo[dy; and] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond and in severe misery.

There are occasions when Sin shall mount up with its foolishness; and it disturbs the consideration, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt in him, and he utters some foo[li]sh words and some [words of falsehood.]

[T]hen, have I taught you, and opened your (sg.) [eyes], as to how confusion shall arise in the zo[ne], in the camps of these great mig[hty] gods? Again, this is how disturbance shall come about, from ti[me] to time, in the [camp] of the [Li]ght [M]ind.
So al[so] these watch-keepers, for they are set [fast and] fi[rm in] the zone, (but) they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of the Light Mind, [for he is] not visible in the body.

Also, [corr]esponding to th[ese] outer [watch-keepers]: in that while they are great, [y]et have they contorted themselves. They have [contracted], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each o[n]e [of t]hem. Again, this too is like the Mind, himse[lf] a great one, and exalted; but he is bent over and [has] become small, to this little worthless [bo]dy.

[Even so] the gods in the outer [z]one: they are transcendent and purified, they are set [f]a[st in] the mingling of the totality, (but) are not defiled. [This too is like the] Light [Mind]. While he is placed in hi[s body, he is not defiled.]

Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of the Light Mind: how vast he is over all the watch-districts of the body! He stays fast at his camp. He shuts off all deliberations of the body from the beguilements of Sin. He limits them and distributes them out. He sets them down at his pleasure.

Also, he does another work, surpassing and ex/ceeding (these). He bestows a great spirit upon the ele/ct one. Indeed, now may you find him, as he stands on the earth, [r]ising up in his heart and ascending to the Father, the G[o]d of truth. He who exists and is established above all the things of loss. [Onc]e again, he may push dow[n] in his insight and his consideration, and descend to the land of Darkness, from where the Darkness has poured forth. His heart shall run and touch everything, as it [passes through all that exists.]
I have taught you the deeds of the [Light] Mind! Whoever has an open and percept[ive] eye, [he can] appear to him. Whoever has not that eye, he can not appear to him.

He has [...] the Keeper of Splendour, the mind that is [...] in the wo[r]ld of the mind that is above. He has [...] whole [...] of the powers of hea[ven that] are in [...] of the great King of Honour, [who is the thought that exists i]n the seventh firmament. He has humbled [...] also of the Adamant of Lig[h]t, who is the insight [... ] from he has given [...] because of lust [... He has] also appointed the King of Glory, who is the coun[sel ...] patience over the three images; that of wind, that of fire, and that of water. He has handed over to him the [...] do evilness. [...] the Porter, who is the consideration [...] the wisdom in the [...] which is below. He has made him [...] the foundation [below ...]

Now, also, happen you know [...] the world is set firm, being ordered [...] the five sons of the Living Spirit in all its members [...]. Sin took this body out from [the] la[nd (?) ... co]nstructed it in its members. It took its [bod]y from the five bodies of darkness. (Sin) constructed the body. Yet, its [sou]l i[t] took from the five shining gods.

Also, the new man reigns by his love, by hi[s] faith, by his perfection, by his patience, and by his wisdom. Yet, his king [...] the Light Mind, he w[ho is] king over the totality. He re[igns] o[ver it according to] his pleasure. While the members [...], thus Sin is imprisoned. Still, the Light Mind is king, and an affliction may arise in the body from t[im]e to time.
